plain_english: Now the third chapter: if your thought holds action superior, O Janardana, then why do you engage me in terrible action, O Kesava?
sanskrit_cite: athaḥ tṛtīyo'dhyāyaḥ   jyāyasī cetkarmaṇaste matā buddhirjanārdana | tatkiṃ karmaṇi  ghore māṃ niyojayasi keśava

plain_english: You seem to confuse my intelligence with mixed speech; speak one decided way by which I may attain the good.
sanskrit_cite: vyāmiśreṇeva vākyena buddhiṃ mohayasīva me | tadekaṃ vada  niścitya yena śreyo'hamāpnuyām | karma uktaṃ jñānaṃ ca | tatra na dvayoḥ prādhānyaṃ yuktam apitu  jñānasya | tadbalena kṣapaṇīyatvaṃ yadi karmaṇāṃ buddhiyukto  jahātīme ityādinayena mūlata eva tat karmaṇā kiṃ prayojanamiti  praśnābhiprāyaḥ

plain_english: The Lord gives a reply: in this world twofold steadfastness was formerly declared by me, O sinless one.
sanskrit_cite: śrībhagavāṃstūttaraṃ dadāti   loke'smindvividhā niṣṭhā purā proktā mayānagha | jñānayogena  sāṅkhyānāṃ karmayogena yoginām | loke eṣā dvayī gatiḥ prasiddhā | sāṃkhyānāṃ jñānaṃ  pradhānaṃ yogināṃ ca karmeti | mayā tu saikaiva niṣṭhoktā  jñānakriyāmayatvātsaṃvittattvasyeti bhāvaḥ | tathāhi-

plain_english: A person does not attain inaction by not beginning actions, nor does he attain perfection by renunciation alone.
sanskrit_cite: na karmaṇāmanārambhānnaiṣkarmyaṃ puruṣo'śnute | na ca  saṃnyasanādeva siddhiṃ samadhigacchati

plain_english: No one ever stands without acting even for a moment; everyone is made to act helplessly by the gunas born of nature.
sanskrit_cite: na hi kaścitkṣaṇamapi jātu tiṣṭhatyakarmakṛt | kāryate  hyavaśaḥ karma sarvaḥ prakṛtijairguṇaiḥ | jñānaṃ karmaṇā rahitaṃ na bhavati karma ca kauśalopetaṃ  jñānarahitaṃ na bhavati ityekameva vastu jñānakarmaṇī | tathā  coktaṃ   na kriyārahitaṃ jñānaṃ na jñānarahitā kriyā | jñānakriyāviniṣpaśca ācāryaḥ paśupāśahā | iti | tasmājjñānāntarvarti karmāparihāryam yataḥ paravaśa eva  kāyavāṅmanasāṃ parispandātmakatvāt avaśyaṃ kiṃcitkaroti

plain_english: He who restrains the action organs yet remembers sense objects by mind is deluded and is called of foolish conduct.
sanskrit_cite: karmendriyāṇi saṃyamya ya āste manasā smaran | indriyārthānvimūḍhātmā mūḍhācāraḥ sa ucyate | karmendriyaiścainna karoti avaśyaṃ tarhi manasā karoti | pratyuta  mūḍhācāraḥ-mānasānāṃ karmaṇāmatyantamaparihāryatvāt

plain_english: One who restrains the senses by mind and begins action-yoga without attachment excels in actions; no knowledge is lost because action proceeds like a machine.
sanskrit_cite: yastvindriyāṇi manasā niyamyārabhate'rjuna | karmendriyaiḥ  karmayogamasaktaḥ sa viśiṣyate | karmasu kriyamāṇeṣu na jñānahāniḥ-manaso'vyāpāre  yantrapuruṣavatkarmaṇaḥ kriyamāṇatvāt

plain_english: Therefore do prescribed action; action is better than inaction, and even body maintenance depends on action.
sanskrit_cite: ataḥ   niyataṃ kuru karma tvaṃ karma jyāyo hyakarmaṇaḥ | śarīrayātrāpi  ca te na prasiddhyedakarmaṇaḥ | niyataṃ-śāstrīyaṃ karma kuru śarīrayātrāmātrasyāpi  karmādhīnatvāt

plain_english: This world is bound by action other than sacrifice; therefore perform action for sacrifice, free from attachment, since obligatory action without fruit-attachment does not yield binding fruit.
sanskrit_cite: yataḥ   yajñārthātkarmaṇo'nyatra loko'yaṃ karmabandhanaḥ | tadarthaṃ  karma kaunteya muktasaṅgaḥ samācara | yajñārthāt-avaśyakaraṇīyāt anyāni karmāṇi bandhakāni | avaśya-kartavyaṃ muktaphalasaṅgatayā kriyamāṇaṃ na phaladam

plain_english: Having created beings with sacrifice, the lord of beings said that through it they should procreate; beings were created together with actions, and actions yield either world-cycle through attachment or liberation through detachment.
sanskrit_cite: sahayajñāḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā purovāca prajāpatiḥ | anena  prasaviṣyadhvameṣa vo'stviṣṭakāmadhuk | prajāpatiḥ-paramātmā prajāḥ sahaiva karmabhiḥ sasarja | uktaṃ ca  tena prajānāṃ karmabhya eva prasavaḥ santānaḥ etānyeva ceṣṭaṃ  saṃsāraṃ mokṣaṃ vā dāsyanti | saṅgātsaṃsāraṃ  muktasaṅgatvānmokṣam

plain_english: Nourish the gods by this action, and they will nourish you; mutual nourishment of gods and senses quickly yields supreme welfare.
sanskrit_cite: yatra yeṣāṃ mokṣaprādhānyaṃ taireva viṣayāḥ sevyā ityucyate   devānbhāvayatānena te devā bhāvayantu vaḥ | parasparaṃ  bhāvayantaḥ śreyaḥ paramavāpsyatha | devāḥ-krīḍanaśīlā indriyavṛttayaḥ karaṇeśvaryo devatā  rahasyaśāstraprasiddhāḥ tā anena karmaṇā  tarpayata-yathāsaṃbhavaṃ viṣayānbhakṣayatetyarthaḥ | tṛptāśca  satyastā vo-yuṣmān ātmana eva svarūpamātrocitāpavargān  bhāvayantu-svātma-sthitiyogyatvāt | evamanavarataṃ  vyutthānasamādhisamayaparamparāyāmindriyatarpaṇatadātma-sādbhāva  lakṣaṇe parasparabhāvane sati śīghrameva paramaṃ  śreyaḥ-parasparabhedavigalanalakṣaṇaṃ brahma prāpsyatha

plain_english: Gods nourished by sacrifice give desired objects; one who enjoys them without returning is a thief, so enjoyments should be used as they arise.
sanskrit_cite: na kevalamitthamapavarge yāvatsiddhilābhe'pyayaṃ mārga ityāha   iṣṭānkāmānhi vo devā dāsyante yajñabhāvitāḥ | tairdattānapradāyaibhyo yo bhuṅkte stena eva saḥ | yajñatarpitāni hīndriyāṇi sthitiṃ badhnanti yatra kvāpi  dhyeyādāviti | ata eva tadvyāpāre sati teṣāṃ viṣayāṇāṃ  smṛtisaṃkalpadhyānādinā bhāvāḥ-viṣayā indriyaireva dattāḥ  yadi teṣāmeva upabhogāya na dīyante tarhi stenatvaṃ-cauryaṃ syāt  chadmacāritvāt | uktaṃ hi pūrvameva bhagavatā mūḍhācāraḥ sa  ucyate iti | ato'yaṃ vākyārthaḥ-yaḥ sukhopāyaṃ siddhimapavargaṃ  vā prepsati tena indriyakautukanivṛtti-mātraphalatayaiva bhogā  yathopanatamāsevyā iti

plain_english: Those who eat the remainder of sacrifice are freed from all sins, while those who cook only for themselves obtain sin.
sanskrit_cite: yajñaśiṣṭāśinaḥ santo mucyante sarvakilbiṣaiḥ | bhuñjate te  tvaghaṃ pāpā ye pacantyātmakāraṇāt | avaśyakartavyatārūpaśāsanamahimāyātānbhogān ye'śnanti  avāntaravyāpāramātratayā ata eva ca  pṛthagphalatvābhāvāṅgatayā | atha  ca-indriyātmakadevagaṇatarpaṇalakṣaṇayajñāt  avaśiṣṭam-antaḥsārasvātmasthityānandalakṣaṇavighasaṃ  ye'śnanti-tatrārūḍhā bhavanti tadupādeyopāyatayā tu  viṣayabhogaṃ vāñchanti te sarvakilviṣaiḥ-śubhāśubhairmucyante | ye tu ātmakāraṇāditi-avidyāvaśāt sthūlameva viṣayabhogaṃ  paratvena manvānāḥ ātmārthamidaṃ vayaṃ kurmaḥ-iti kurvate | ta  eva aghaṃ-śubhāśubhātmakaṃ labhante

plain_english: Beings arise from food, food from rain, rain from sacrifice, and sacrifice from action.
sanskrit_cite: annād bhavanti bhūtāni parjanyādannasambhavaḥ | yajñād bhavati  parjanyo yajñaḥ karmasamudbhavaḥ

plain_english: Know action as born from brahman and brahman from the imperishable; all-pervading brahman is eternally established in sacrifice.
sanskrit_cite: karma brahmodbhavaṃ viddhi brahmākṣarasamudbhavam | tasmāt  sarvagataṃ brahma nityaṃ yajñe pratiṣṭhitam | annāt-avibhāgabhogyasvabhāvāt  kathañcinmāyāvidyākālādyanekāparaparyāyāt bhūtāni vicitrāṇi  bhavanti | taccānnaṃ parjanyāt-avicchinnasaṃvitsvabhāvādātmanaḥ  bhoktṛtantrātmalābhatvādbhogyatāyāḥ | sa ca parjanyo-bhoktā  yajñāt bhogakriyāyattatvādbhoktṛtvasya | bhogakriyā ca  karmaṇaḥ-kriyāśaktisvātantryabalāt | tacca  svātantryam-avicchinnamapi  anavacchinnānantasvātantryapūrṇasamucchalanmaheśvarabhāvaparamātm  a-brahmasaṃsparśavaśāt | tacca ucchaladacchānācchāditaiśvaryaṃ  brahma-akṣarāt-praśāntāśeṣaiśvaryataraṅgātsaṃvinmātrāt | ityevaṃ suvyavasthito'yaṃ yajñaḥ ṣaḍaraṃ cakraṃ vāhayan  arātrayasandhānādapavargam  arātrayatantraṇādvyavahāramāsūtrayati | iti  vidyāvidyollāsataraṅgasubhagaṃ brahma yajñe eva pratiṣṭhitam | anye tu-annaṃ tāvadvīryalohitakrameṇa bhūtakāraṇam annaṃ ca  vṛṣṭidvāreṇa parjanyāt so'pi yajñāt yajñaḥ kriyātaḥ sā ca  jñānapūrvikā jñānamakṣarāt iti | apare tu-annam-adyamānaṃ  viṣayapañcakamāśritya bhūtāni-indriyāṇi  viṣayāścātmasphuritarūpāḥ | ata ātmaiva viṣayopabhogena | poṣyate | ataśca sarvagataṃ brahma karmaṇi  pratiṣṭhitam-tanmayatvāttasya

plain_english: One who does not follow this wheel lives in vain, and one who delights only in the senses is full of sin.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ pravartitaṃ cakraṃ nānuvartayatīha yaḥ | aghāyurindriyārāmo moghaṃ pārtha sa jīvati | yastvevaṃ nāṅgīkaroti sa pāpamayaḥ | yataḥ sa indriyeṣveva  ramate nātmani

plain_english: For a human who delights in the self and is self-satisfied, no duty remains.
sanskrit_cite: yaścātmaratireva syādātmatṛptaśca mānavaḥ | ātmanyeva ca  santuṣṭastasya kāryaṃ na vidyate

plain_english: For him no purpose arises from action or nonaction, and he acts without dependence on purpose in beings.
sanskrit_cite: naiva tasya kṛtenārtho nākṛteneha kaścana | na cāsya  sarvabhūteṣu kaścidarthavyapāśrayaḥ | ātmaratestu-karmendriyavyāpāratayaiva kurvataḥ karaṇākaraṇeṣu  samatā | ata eva nāsau bhūteṣu kiṃcidātmaprayojanamapekṣya  nigrahānugrahau karoti apitu karaṇīyamidam-ityetāvatā

plain_english: Janaka and others attained perfection through action; seeing world-welfare, you too should act, and they remain examples for those acting toward perfection.
sanskrit_cite: karmaṇaiva hi saṃsiddhimāsthitā janakādayaḥ | lokasaṃgrahamevāpi  sampaśyankartumarhasi | tadatra kurvatāmapi siddhau janakādayo dṛṣṭāntāḥ

plain_english: Whatever the best person does, others do; whatever standard he sets, the world follows.
sanskrit_cite: yadyadācarati śreṣṭhastattadevetaro janaḥ | sa yatpramāṇaṃ  kurute lokastadanuvartate

plain_english: O Partha, I have no duty in the three worlds, nothing unattained to attain, yet I engage in action.
sanskrit_cite: na me pārthāsti kartavyaṃ triṣu lokeṣu kiñcana | nānavāptamavāptavyaṃ pravarte'tha ca karmaṇi

plain_english: If I did not ever act unweariedly, people would follow my path in every way, O Partha.
sanskrit_cite: yadi hyahaṃ na varteyaṃ jātu karmaṇyatandritaḥ | mama  vartmānuvarteranmanuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ

plain_english: These worlds would perish if I did not act; I would become maker of confusion and harm these beings.
sanskrit_cite: utsīdeyurime lokā na kuryāṃ karma cedaham | saṅkarasya ca kartā  syāmupahanyāmimāḥ prajāḥ

plain_english: Therefore, always perform duty unattached; for an unattached person performing action attains the supreme.
sanskrit_cite: tasmādasaktaḥ satataṃ kāryaṃ karma samācara | asakto  hyācarankarma paramāpnoti pūruṣaḥ

plain_english: As the unwise act attached, the wise should act unattached for the gathering of the world.
sanskrit_cite: saktāḥ karmaṇyavidvāṃso yathā kurvanti bhārata | kuryādvidvāṃstathāsaktaścikīrṣurlokasaṃgraham | prāptaprāpaṇīyasya paripūrṇamanaso'pi karmapravṛttau  lokānugrahaḥ prayojanam-ityatra śrībhagavānātmānameva  dṛṣṭāntamakaroti | tasmādasakta eva karaṇīyaṃ karma kuryāt | kiṃca viditavedyaḥ | karma cet tyajet tallokānāṃ durbheda  evaikaprasiddhapakṣaśithilitāsthābandhatvenāprarūḍhilakṣaṇo  jāyate | yataḥ karmavāsanāṃ ca na moktuṃ śaknuvanti  jñānadhārāṃ ca nāśrayitum | atha ca śithilībhavanti

plain_english: The wise should not disturb the intellect of the ignorant, but engage all actions properly.
sanskrit_cite: yataste na samyagjñānena pūtāḥ ato buddherbhedanaṃ-vicālanaṃ  teṣāṃ paramo'nartha ityanugrahāya bhedayenna dhiyameṣām tadāha   na buddhibhedaṃ janayedajñānāṃ karmasaṅginām | joṣayet  sarvakarmāṇi vidvānyuktaḥ samācaran | svayaṃ caivaṃ buddhyamānaḥ karmāṇi kuryāt | na ca lokānāṃ  buddhiṃ bhindyād

plain_english: The deluded self thinks itself the doer and binds itself falsely.
sanskrit_cite: ajñānamityuktaṃ tadajñatvaṃ darśayati   prakṛteḥ kriyamāṇāni guṇaiḥ karmāṇi bhāgaśaḥ | ahaṅkāravimūḍhātmā kartāhamiti manyate | prakṛtisaṃbandhibhirguṇaiḥ sattvādyaiḥ kila karmāṇi kriyante | mūḍhaścāhaṃ kartetyadhyavasya mithyaivātmānaṃ badhnāti

plain_english: Knowing the distinction of strands and action, one does not attach.
sanskrit_cite: tattvavittu mahābāho guṇakarmavibhāgayoḥ | guṇā guṇeṣu vartanta  iti matvā na sajjate | guṇakarmavibhāgatattvavittu prakṛtiḥ karoti mama  kimāyātam-ityātmānaṃ mocayati

plain_english: Deluded by nature's strands, people attach to actions; the united should engage in them.
sanskrit_cite: karmasaṅgināmityuktam tat karmasaṅgitvaṃ darśayati   prakṛterguṇasammūḍhāḥ sajjante guṇakarmasu | tānakṛtsnavido  mandānkṛtsnavinna vicālayet | prakṛtisaṃbandhibhirguṇaiḥ satvādyaiḥ kṛteṣu karmaṣu mūḍhāḥ  sajjanti sattvādiguṇamāhātmyāt | tasmādyuktaḥ san juṣeta  karmāṇi ityuktam | tatra katham iti sphuṭayati-

plain_english: Renouncing all actions to me, fight desireless and mineless for world grace.
sanskrit_cite: mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṃnyasyādhyātmacetasā | nirāśīrnirmamo  bhūtvā yudhyasva vigatajvaraḥ | mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi nāhaṃ kartā-iti saṃnyasya svatantraḥ  parameśvara eva sarvakartā nāhaṃ kaścit-iti niścitya  lokānugrahaṃ cikīrṣurlokācāraṃ yuddhātmakamanutiṣṭha

plain_english: Those faithful humans who always practice this teaching are freed from all actions; whoever relies on it and does anything is not bound.
sanskrit_cite: ye me matamidaṃ nityamanutiṣṭhanti mānavāḥ | śraddhāvanto'nasūyanto mucyante sarvakarmabhiḥ | etacca matamāśritya yaḥ kaścidyatkiṃcitkaroti tattasya na bandhakam

plain_english: Those who disparage and do not follow this teaching are deluded and lost; the unfaithful in this knowledge are destroyed continuously because of fear of birth and death.
sanskrit_cite: ye tvetadabhyasūyanto nānuvartanti me matam | sarvajñānavimūḍhāṃstānviddhi naṣṭānacetasaḥ | etasmiṃstu jñāne ye na śraddhālavaste vinaṣṭāḥ-avirataṃ  janmamaraṇādibhayabhāvitatvāt

plain_english: Even the knower acts according to his own nature; beings go to nature and dissolve there, so what can restraint do? Even the knower shows no reversal in conduct such as eating, but acts fittingly; since beings dissolve in nature and the self is non-agent and eternally free, whose birth and so on can be restrained? How then is there bondage? Thus it is said.
sanskrit_cite: sadṛśaṃ ceṣṭate svasyāḥ prakṛterjñānavānapi | prakṛtiṃ  yānti bhūtāni nigrahaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati | yo'pi ca jñānī na tasya vyavahāre bhojanādau viparyāsaḥ kaścit  apitu so'pi sattvādyucitameva ceṣṭate | evameva jānan yato  bhūtānāṃ-pṛthivyādīnāṃ prakṛtau vilayaḥ ātmā cākartā  nityamuktaḥ iti kasya janmādinigrahaḥ | kathaṃ tarhi bandhaḥ ? itthamucyate-

plain_english: For each sense in its object, attraction and aversion are established; one should not come under their sway, for they are obstacles to him.
sanskrit_cite: indriyasyendriyasyārthe rāgadveṣau vyavasthitau | tayorna  vaśamāgacchettau hyasya paripanthinau

plain_english: One's own duty, though flawed, is better than another's well performed; death in one's own duty is better than another's arising. The world-bound one grasps attraction and aversion toward each object, regarding actions as self-performed through delusion. Even equally in eating and conduct, the knowing and world-bound differ. Our settled doctrine: for one freed from attachment and practicing own duty, no merit-demerit bondage exists, since own duty does not depart from the heart and is rooted in one's own nature; thus no creature is born empty, so it is not to be abandoned.
sanskrit_cite: śreyān svadharmo viguṇaḥ paradharmātsvanuṣṭhitāt | svadharme  nidhanaṃ śreyaḥ paradharmodayādapiḥ | saṃsārī ca prativiṣayaṃ rāgaṃ dveṣaṃ ca gṛhṇāti | yataḥ  karmāṇi ātmakartṛkāṇyeva vimūḍhatvādabhimanyate iti samamapi  bhojanādivyavahāraṃ kurvatorjñānisaṃsāriṇorastyayaṃ viśeṣaḥ | ayaṃ naḥ siddhāntaḥ-sarvathā muktasaṃgasya svadharmacāriṇo  nāsti kaścitpuṇyapāpātmako bandhaḥ | svadharmo hi  hṛdayādanapāyī svarasanirūḍha eva | na tena kaścidapi rikto  janturjāyate-ityatyājyaḥ

plain_english: Arjuna asks by what impelled a person commits sin even unwillingly, as if forced, and how a person proceeds knowing it as sin. The question's arising has this intent: if own duty does not depart from the heart, how can unrighteous conduct be this? What is this own duty by which a creature is said to be empty? Here the answer: even though own duty is in the heart, this disturbance is made by a foreign covering, not by its absence.
sanskrit_cite: arjuna uvāca   atha kena prayukto'yaṃ pāpaṃ carati pūruṣaḥ | anicchamano'pi  balādākramyeva niyojitaḥ | pāpaṃ pāpatayā vidannapi janaḥ kathaṃ tatra pravartate ? iti  praśnaḥ | asya praśnasyotthāne'yamāśayaḥ-svadharmo yadi  svahṛdayādanapāyitvādatyājyaḥ kathaṃ  tarhyadharmācaraṇameṣāmiti | ko'yaṃ svadharmo nāma yenārikto  jantuḥ-ityuktaṃ bhavati | atrottaraṃ satyapi svadharme hṛdisthe āgantukāvaraṇakṛto'yaṃ  vilpavaḥ na tu tadabhāvakṛtaḥ-ityāśayena-

plain_english: Kṛṣṇa says desire and anger, born of rajas, are the great devourer and sin-giver; the wise should know this enemy.
sanskrit_cite: śrībhagavānuvāca   kāma eṣa krodha eṣa rajoguṇasamudbhavaḥ | mahāśano mahāpāpmā  viddhyenamiha vairiṇam | dvābhyāmetacchabdābhyāmanayoratyantāvaiṣamyaṃ sūcyate etau ca  kāmakrodhau nityasaṃbandhināvanyonyāvinābhāvena vartete  ityekarūpatayaiva vyācaṣṭe | eṣa ca mahasya-   sukhasya aśano-grāsakārakaḥ mahataḥ pāpasya hetutvācca krodha eva  pāpadāyī | enaṃ ca vairiṇaṃ prājño jānīyāt

plain_english: Arjuna asks Kṛṣṇa how this enemy arises, grows, what it is, and what it does.
sanskrit_cite: nanu arthādyupaghātakaṃ jñātasvarūpaṃ ca vastu hātuṃ suśakaṃ  bhavet-ityabhiprāyeṇārjuna uvāca   bhavatyeṣa kathaṃ kṛṣṇa kathaṃ caiva vivardhate | kimātmakaḥ  kimācārastanmamācakṣva pṛcchataḥ | asya cotpattau kiṃ kāraṇaṃ vardhane ca ko hetuḥ svarūpaṃ cāsya  kīdṛk utpannau rūḍhībhūtaśca kimācarati-kiṃ karoti ? iti  praśnāḥ | atrottaraṃ-

plain_english: Kṛṣṇa says the enemy is subtle and supreme, deluding Pārtha through the senses, though truly sorrow and delusion.
sanskrit_cite: śrībhagavānuvāca   eṣa sūkṣmaḥ paraḥ śatrurdehināmindriyaiḥ saha | sukhatantra  ivāsīno mohayanpārtha tiṣṭhati | eṣa tāvatsūkṣmaḥ-utpattisamaye'lakṣya indriyeṣu | evaṃ ca  vartamānaḥ sukhaṃ tantrayitumivotpadyate vastutastu  duḥkhamohamayaḥ-tāmasatvāt | ata eva mohayan

plain_english: Desire and anger become a terrible ego of pride and joy, hard to cross through sinful actions.
sanskrit_cite: kāmakrodhamayo ghoraḥ stambhaharṣasamudbhavaḥ | ahaṅkāro'bhimānātmā dustaraḥ pāpakarmabhiḥ | stambhaḥ-kulādyabhimānaḥ tatkṛto yo harṣaḥ-ahamīdṛśaḥ-iti | ata evāha-ahaṃkāra iti

plain_english: The enemy turns away joy, gives grief, makes fear, and deludes repeatedly; pride grows ego-nature through pleasure-thought.
sanskrit_cite: harṣamasya nivartyaiṣa śokamasya dadāti ca | bhayaṃ cāsya  karotyeṣa mohayaṃstu muhurmuhuḥ | ata eva ca garvādvardhate'bhimānasvabhāvaḥ sukhabuddhiprakāreṇa  ca jāyate iti trayaḥ praśnāḥ parihṛtāḥ

plain_english: The enemy is impure, fault-seeking, rajas-driven delusion that destroys this and other worlds by faults.
sanskrit_cite: sa eṣa kaluṣī kṣudraśchidraprekṣī dhanañjaya | rajaḥpravṛtto  mohātmā manuṣyāṇāmupadravaḥ | sa eṣa iti cchidrāṇi prekṣate-amunā cchidreṇāsyehalokaparalokau  nāśayāmi-iti | tathā ca mokṣadharmeṣu | arjuna uvāca   yatkrodhano yajate yaddadāti yadvā tapastapyate yajjuhoti | vaivasvatastaddharate'sya sarvaṃ moghaḥ śramo bhavati krodhanasya | iti | rajasaḥ pravṛttastamorūpa ityarthaḥ

plain_english: Just as fire is covered by smoke, a mirror by dust, and an embryo by the womb, so this self is covered by that. Through these three examples are said its hard-to-remove quality, its doing of forbidden acts, and its being a seat of disgust: this is the self.
sanskrit_cite: dhūmenāvriyate vahniryathā''darśo malena ca | yatholvenāvṛto  garbhastathā nenāyamāvṛtaḥ | dṛṣṭāntatrayeṇa durapasarpatvam akāryakaratvaṃ yugupsāspadatvaṃ  coktam | ayamiti-ātmā

plain_english: Knowledge is covered by desire, the knower's eternal enemy, O Kaunteya—an insatiable fire that roams through the senses and burns both seen and unseen, never to be filled.
sanskrit_cite: āvṛtaṃ jñānametena jñānino nityavairiṇā | kāmarūpeṇa  kaunteya duṣpūreṇānalena ca | kāmarūpa icchāyāṃ yataścarati | analena ca-agnineva  pūrayitumaśakyena-dṛṣṭādṛṣṭadvayadāhakatvāt

plain_english: The senses, mind, and intellect are said to be the seat of the embodied being; through them he deludes the embodied one by covering knowledge. First, when the senses are present, it stands; just as an enemy seen by the eye generates anger in the sense-region itself, then in the mind's determination, then in the intellect's certainty; by this means, generating delusion, he destroys knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: indriyāṇi mano buddhirasyādhiṣṭhānamucyate | etairvimohayatyeṣa  jñānamāvṛtya dehinam | ādau indriyeṣu satsu tiṣṭhati | yathā cakṣuṣā śatrurdṛṣṭa  indriyapradeśe eva krodhamātmano janayati | tato manasi-saṃkalpe | tato buddhau-niścaye | etadvāreṇa mohaṃ janayan jñānaṃ nāśayati

plain_english: To prevent this evil, first restrain the senses, O best of Bharatas, and abandon the evil that destroys knowledge and realization; do not first grasp knowledge of Brahman, realization, or divine-filled action, since it destroys; therefore abandon anger; or, having prevented destruction by knowledge-mind and realization-intellect, do not grasp what arises in the senses as intention, nor determine the intended.
sanskrit_cite: asya nivāraṇe upāyamāha   tasmāttvamindriyāṇyādau niyamya bharatarṣabha | pāpmānaṃ  prajahīhyenaṃ jñānavijñānanāśanam | tasmādādāvindriyāṇi niyamayet-krodhādikamindriyeṣu prathamaṃ na  gṛhṇīyāt | jñānaṃ-brahma vijñānaṃ ca-bhagavanmayīṃ kriyāṃ  nāśayati | hi-yataḥ ataḥ pāpmānaṃ krodhaṃ tyaja | athavā-jñānena-manasā vijñānena-buddhyā ca nāśanaṃ-vāraṇaṃ  kṛtvā iti kriyāviśeṣaṇam indriyeṣūtpannaṃ saṃkalpe na  gṛhṇīyāt | saṃkalpitaṃ vā na niścinuyāditi tātparyam

plain_english: Here the method is stated in two verses: the senses are called superior; beyond the senses is the mind; beyond the mind is intelligence; and beyond intelligence is he.
sanskrit_cite: atra yuktiṃ ślokadvayenāha   indriyāṇi parāṇyāhurindriyebhyaḥ paraṃ manaḥ | manasastu parā  buddhiryo buddheḥ paratastu saḥ

plain_english: Thus, having known what is beyond intellect and steadied oneself by oneself, slay the enemy, mighty-armed, formed of desire and hard to approach. The senses are other than sense-objects marked as enemy; mind is other than them; intellect is distinct even from mind; and the self is that whose nature is other. How can anger born of the senses agitate mind, intellect, or self? Thus consider. The intent of secret knowers is that intellect abides elsewhere; supreme ego is all-I identity-nature, supreme nonduality. Because the full has no fragmentation, anger and the rest do not arise. Therefore, grasping supreme ego—other-enthusiasm, consciousness-natured anger, ignorance-natured enemy—slay it; auspicious.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ buddheḥ paraṃ buddhvā saṃstabhyātmānamātmanā | jahi  śatruṃ mahābāho kāmarūpaṃ durāsadam | yata indriyāṇi śatrulakṣaṇādviṣayādanyāni | tebhyaścānyanmanaḥ | tasmādapi buddhervyatirekaḥ | buddherapi  yasyānyasvabhāvatvaṃ sa ātmā | evamindriyotpannena krodhena kathaṃ  manaso buddherātmano vā kṣobhaḥ ? iti paryālocayedityarthaḥ | rahasyavidāṃ tvayamāśayaḥ-buddheryaḥ paratra vartate  paro'haṃkāraḥ-sarvamaham-ityabhedātmā sa khalu paramo'bhedaḥ | ata eva ca paripūrṇasya khaṇḍanābhāvānna krodhādaya udayante | ataḥ paramahaṃkāraṃ-parotsāhasaṃvidātmakaṃ gṛhītvā krodham  avidyātmānaṃ śatruṃ jahīti śivam

plain_english: Here is the summary verse: what can anger and other mind-delusions do to one who regards wife, body, and dense things as other? Thus ends the third chapter of Abhinavagupta's Gita Meaning Gathering.
sanskrit_cite: atra saṃgrahaślokaḥ   ghanāni dārāndehaṃ ca yo'nyatvenādhigacchati | kiṃ nāma tasya  kurvanti krodhādyāścittavibhramāḥ | iti  śrīmahāmāheśvarācāryavaryarājānakābhinavaguptapādaviracite  śrīmadbhagavadgītārthasaṃgrahe tṛtīyo'dhyāyaḥ
